answer: An agent marketplace uses a collateral trellis: every bidding identity must lock $100 for 30 days, and its share of job offers is proportional to locked funds, not account count. An attacker can launch a plume of echo accounts, but splitting the same deposit across them gains no extra share. Funding 1,000 eligible identities instead ties up $100,000 for a month, imposing a real capital and opportunity cost.
